A.explanation: Force $120 \text{ N}$ through $0.25 \text{ m}$ gives $W = 120 \times 0.25 = 30 \text{ J}$.

B.explanation: This value is 100 times too large and results from converting only one of the $\text{cm}$ quantities to $\text{m}$.

C.explanation: This value results from using $400 \text{ cm}^2$ and $25 \text{ cm}$ directly with $3000 \text{ Pa}$ without any conversion to metres.

D.explanation: This value is far too large and results from mishandling the $\text{cm}^2$ to $\text{m}^2$ conversion and powers of ten.

hints: Notice the area is $400 \text{ cm}^2$ and the distance is $25 \text{ cm}$, while pressure is $3000 \text{ Pa}$ in SI units, so both lengths need conversion to metres.
Connect pressure to force with $p = F/A$, giving $F = pA$, then link that constant force to work with $W = Fd$.
Calculate the swept volume change $A \times d$ in $\text{m}^3$ first, then use $W = p\Delta V$ and check the power of ten carefully.
walkthrough: Identify the physics: the piston pushes against fixed pressure $p = 3000 \text{ Pa}$, so the force is $F = pA$ and the work for distance $d$ is $W = Fd = pAd$.
Convert to SI units: $A = 400 \text{ cm}^2 = 400 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2 = 0.040 \text{ m}^2$ and $d = 25 \text{ cm} = 0.25 \text{ m}$.
Calculate the work: $W = Fd = 120 \times 0.25 = 30 \text{ J}$, which is also $W = p\Delta V = 3000 \times 0.010 = 30 \text{ J}$ with $\Delta V = 0.010 \text{ m}^3$.
The unit check gives $\text{Pa} \times \text{m}^3 = \text{N m} = \text{J}$, and $30 \text{ J}$ matches the given option. This is option A.
